name: Xenazoic Acid

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in France and Belgium, first in 1965 — for liver harm

summary: Xenazoic Acid was pulled from the market in France and Belgium starting in 1965 because it caused liver harm [3]. In addition, a small computer model rather than tests on people estimated its risk scores, rating its liver risk as medium with a score of 57 [M]. The same computer model rated the drug's heart risk as low with a score of 21 [M].
